MINUTES
  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING
  AUGUST 15, 2018

1.  CALL TO ORDER

  CHAIR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

  Committee Members Present:  Chair Schmitz, Combs, Lum, Pope, Scott, Vanden
  Bos, Wisot

  Committee Members Absent:  Munday

  Staff Members Present:  Greg Grammer, Assistant City Manager
  Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineering Deputy, Willdan
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  Also Present:  Sgt. Ricky Osburn, LACSD, Lomita Station
  Deputy Tami Bouse, LACSD, Lomita Station

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A motion was made to approve minutes of the Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting of
  March 14, 2018 as presented.

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

  None

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  DAPPLEGRAY SCHOOL AND DAPPLEGRAY LANE PROPERTY OWNERS
  ASSOCIATION – TRAFFIC CONCERNS ALONG PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH
  Assistant City Manager Grammer introduced Item 5-A, and stated that staff met with two
  parents regarding traffic and speeding concerns on Palos Verdes Drive North (PVDN).
  Following that meeting, staff received a letter from Dapplegray Elementary School
  principal and the Dapplegray Lane Property Owners Association. More recently, a letter
  stating similar concerns was received from the Montessori School.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a PowerPoint presentation with an overview
  of the traffic concerns and the city’s response. Speeding concerns have been enforced
  by the Sheriff’s Department and include the presence of a decoy vehicle and the radar
  trailer. School zones are identified on PVDN and Rolling Hills Road indicating the speed
  limit of 25 mph. The speed limit of 40 mph on PVDN is set according to the results of the
  engineering and traffic survey which is done every 5-7 years.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that there was a concern with crosswalks and
  stated that there are locations in the city with in-roadway warning lights. An explanation
  was provided regarding the criteria for installation of in-roadway warning lights.

  The City through a services contract with LA County Department of Public Works repaints
  crosswalks on an annual basis prior to the start of the school year. Traffic Engineering
  Deputy Itagaki stated that the concerns with signal timing has been responded to by
  extending the timing for vehicles exiting the school. Once the signal loop detector for
  Dapplegray School is repaired, the signal timing will return to the original timing.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that a suggestion was made to install a flashing
  beacon above the 25 mph during school hours sign to remind people of the speed limit.
  An option of using a radar speed sign was discussed where motorists would see a sign to
  slow down if they are travelling over the posted speed limit. A suggestion was also made
Meeting Minutes
Traffic & Safety Committee
August 15, 2018  1
   for a crossing guard at PVDN and the school, however, the criteria for the number of
  pedestrians crossing during each of any 2 peak hours may not be met. A detailed study
  can be done in order to determine if the guidelines can be satisfied.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that staff recommends that the Traffic and Safety
  Committee provide staff with direction on how to proceed.

  Jennifer Whynaucht, Hitching Post, stated that prior to the construction on PVDN there
  were accidents greater than fender benders. Ms. Whynaucht stated that she has personal
  experience and video documentation showing her and other kids walking to and from
  school while drivers are not paying attention to the posted speed limit and is
  recommending that the rectangular rapid flashing beacons or radar road signs be installed.
  During the two weeks that that the large speed board was out, drivers were slowing down,
  and it also calls attention to school signs. Assistant City Manager stated that the speed
  boards are placed in various neighborhoods throughout the city.

  In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER POPE, Traffic Engineering Deputy
  Itagaki stated that the intent of a flashing beacon or the radar speed sign is that it would
  only be on during school hours to reinforce to motorists the speed limit when children are
  present.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that there are too many signs making it difficult read.
  COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS added that near his street there are two signs
  within 25 feet of each other.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS stated that the radar speed signs are effective.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT stated that from PVDE to Crenshaw, he has counted 38
  signs. He suggested that the speed trailer be brought out when school starts on
  PVDN/PVDE temporarily and then bring it back in a month or two. COMMITTEE MEMBER
  SCHMITZ agreed but also stated that the number of signs need to be evaluated.

  In response to a question by Deputy Bouse, Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that
  the speed board that the city owns may not record vehicle speed. Sgt. Osburn stated that
  there are speed boards that collect data including license plates.

  In response to a question by CHAIR MEMBER SCHMITZ, Assistant Manager Grammer
  stated that after the installation of the median on PVDN, a traffic study was conducted and
  determined that vehicles were travelling at a lower rate of speed and therefore, the speed
  limit was reduced to 35 mph.

  The committee members discussed their opinions on reviewing the posted signs.
  Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that at the next meeting staff will present a
  schedule for the speed board and an inventory of the signs. Traffic Engineering Deputy
  Itagaki added that there are companies that rent speed trailers that store data.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ summarized that for the next Traffic and Safety Committee meeting staff
  will prepare an inventory of signs; rotating schedule locations for the speed trailer; the cost
  of adding radar collection data to the speed trailer; and information and cost related to
  removing signs and adding flashing beacons.
B.  IN-ROADWAY WARNING LIGHTS ON PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND
  ROLLING HILLS ROAD

  Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that in-roadway warning lights were installed at
  PVDN and Rolling Hills Road and there was concern from the Equestrian Committee
  whether they were working. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that lights are
  working properly. There were concerns with the location of the 35 mph speed limit sign
  and it was determined that it was in the correct location, however, could be moved north
  of the crosswalk if desired. There were concerns with landscaping on the east side of the
  street, and maintenance has trimmed back the vegetation to allow better visibility. There
  was also a suggestion to change the yellow flashing lights to red, however, they are
  required to flash yellow.

Meeting Minutes
Traffic & Safety Committee
August 15, 2018  2
   Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that staff recommends that the landscaping
  continue to be monitored and trimmed as needed and that the in-roadway warning lights
  continue flashing yellow.
C.  PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST – CONSIDERATION OF BIKE LANE INSTALLATION

  Assistant City Manager Grammer introduced Item 5-C, consideration for the installation of
  bike lanes on Palos Verdes Drive East (PVDE). Some options would be, to install in-street
  6’ wide bike lanes, which would require widening of the street; or, rolled curb gutter; or, to
  add medians.
  In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT, Assistant Manager
  Grammer stated that the bike lane would be on PVDE from PVDN to the city’s boundary
  going north.
  In response to a comment by CHAIR SCHMITZ, Assistant Manager Grammer stated that
  there are currently no funds available for this project, but it is good to have a conceptual
  design when grants become available.
  A discussion ensued regarding the location of the bike lane.
  COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
  LUM to,

  APPROVE THAT STAFF STUDY THE POSSIBILITY OF MODIFYING PVDE TO
  ACCOMMODATE BIKE LANES ON BOTH SIDES AND PRODUCE A
  CONCEPTUAL DESIGN.

  Ayes: Chair Schmitz, Combs, Lum, Pope, Scott, Vanden Bos, Wisot
  Noes:
  Absent: Munday
  Abstain:

D.  PARKING RESTRICTION ON DEEP VALLEY DRIVE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Assistant City Manager Grammer stated that the owners of the dry cleaners relocated the
  business and the green curb will no longer be pursued.
E.  CALWATER PV PIPELINE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Assistant City Manager Grammer thanked everyone for their patience with the closure of
  the eastbound lane of PVDN. The project will continue east on PVDN and the eastbound
  lane will shift to the opposite side of the raised median. There will be one lane of travel in
  each direction with both lanes on the north side of PVDN separated by tall
  delineators/cones.
  COMMITTEE MEMBER SCHMITZ thanked Assistant City Manager Grammer and staff
  for making sure that this project is on schedule and stated that she is grateful for the way
  that this project is being managed.
  In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT, Assistant Manager
  Grammer stated that the construction hours are from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. Traffic Engineering
  Deputy Itagaki explained how traffic will be controlled.
6.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

  None

7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  COMMITTEE MEMBER WISOT stated that he had brought up the issue of coyotes and
  sadly reported that his 5 lb. Pomeranian was killed by a coyote two weeks later.
  COMMITTEE MEMBER SCHMITZ shared that two cycles of traps were set-up at her
  property by the County and no coyotes were caught, and attributed this to their aptitude in
  regards to the traps. COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT stated that he has witnessed
  coyotes harassing bigger dogs.

Meeting Minutes
Traffic & Safety Committee
August 15, 2018  3
   COMMITTEE MEMBER SCHMITZ stated that if there are coyote sightings, the County
  can send someone to survey private properties and provide recommendations.
  COMMITTEE MEMBER POPE asked about the coyote education program. Assistant City
  Manager Grammer stated that a Wildlife Watch program is in place and consists of a
  hazing team of trained volunteers.
  COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS stated that the vegetation on the walking path at
  PVDN and Silver Spur on the church side needs to be trimmed back.
8.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting at 7:18 p.m.
